sections.h2: Marion, next door to Cedar Rapids
sections.html:
Marion is a Linn County city that sits right beside Cedar Rapids and belongs to the Cedar Rapids metro area. It was incorporated in 1837 and takes its name from Francis Marion, a Revolutionary War figure. The ZIP code is 52302 and the elevation is about 840 feet.

The site was chosen in 1839 as the first county seat of the newly organized Linn County, until a 1919 vote moved the seat to Cedar Rapids, 9,960 to 4,823. The older streets near the Granger House Museum still show how early the town was laid out. Expect a mix on the market, with older uptown houses on one side and subdivisions from the growth years on the other.

Traffic runs north and south on U.S. Route 151 and Iowa Highway 13, and Seventh Avenue leads toward Cedar Rapids. Easy access can come with road noise, so know how far your house is from those routes.

The population stood at 26,294 in 2000, 34,768 in 2010 and 41,535 in 2020, an increase near 58 percent, and mid-2025 brought an estimate of 42,732. Few Iowa cities have grown this fast.

With 77.4 percent of houses owner-occupied, most Marion homes are lived in by their owners. Rentals are a smaller slice, but the city regulates them closely, as the rental section below explains.

Marion is split among three public districts, Marion Independent, Linn-Mar Community and Cedar Rapids Community. Marion Independent covers the south and east sides, while Linn-Mar covers the north, west and far east sides and runs Linn-Mar High School. St. Joseph School, founded in 1947, serves preschool through eighth grade, and Grace Baptist School serves kindergarten through twelfth grade.

Two houses a few blocks apart can sit in different districts, and families often ask first. Confirm the right one for your street with the district itself.

Iowa's temperature swings wear on roofs, gutters, furnaces and basements. An inspector is likely to check the attic's airflow, ice damage along the eaves and any moisture downstairs. The county also went through the June 2008 Cedar River flooding and the August 2020 derecho, so many buyers ask about past storm repairs and whether claims were paid.

If you own a house with deferred roof or basement work, a cash sale as is lets you skip repair bids and the back and forth over inspection credits.

Marion requires owners to register rental units and hold a landlord license, and every rental dwelling is subject to inspection roughly every two years. The city counts a unit as a rental even when family or friends live there without paying rent. Single-family houses, rooming houses and group residences are all covered.

The city charges fees for licenses, inspections, missed inspections and confirmed complaints. Call Marion Rental Housing at 319-200-1299 for the current amounts.

  • Register a new rental, or tell the city you no longer have one.
  • Finish the online landlord license renewal, because no license is issued without it.
  • Expect an inspection about every two years, plus extra visits after complaints.

A landlord selling a tenant-occupied house may need to tell the city the unit is no longer theirs, and a buyer who plans to rent it will have to register it. Under Iowa Code 364.17, a city that adopts a rental program must include regular inspections, may charge reasonable fees and can add a late penalty and interest. Unpaid amounts can become a lien on the property after notice.

The county sends two property tax bills a year, with halves due on September 1 and March 1. Whatever is unpaid goes delinquent on October 1 or April 1. If you mail a check, enclose the stub and make sure it is postmarked by September 30 or March 31, or a late fee follows.

The Linn County Treasurer is at 935 Second Street SW in Cedar Rapids. Payment options are Iowataxandtags.org, the mail, a counter visit, the phone at 319-892-5500, and the drop box outside the Public Service Center. The dates come from Iowa Code 445.37, which pushes delinquency to the second business day of the month if the day before is a weekend day.

At closing, the title company normally works out which share of the current installment is yours and which is the buyer's. Ask for the paid receipts so you know nothing is left behind.

Once signed, the deed goes to the county recorder, together with a declaration of value signed by at least one buyer or seller. Iowa Code 428A.1 adds a transfer tax of 80 cents for every $500 of value past the first $500. It is paid as the deed is handed in, and the amount follows the price actually paid.

  • Signed deed
  • Declaration of value
  • Transfer tax at recording
  • Payoff letters for any mortgage or lien
  • Tax proration between buyer and seller

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Marion house work?
sections.html:
In a cash sale the buyer pays outright. Nothing waits on a lender's appraisal or underwriting. You request an offer, the buyer reviews the house and its title, and you decide. A title company then sets closing for a date that works for you.

That can matter in Marion if the house needs work, has a tenant with a lease or came to you through an estate. Owners who dislike showings and open houses tend to like it too. Because repairs are priced into the offer, the fair comparison is your net from a listing once repairs, commissions and months on the market are subtracted.

No price is promised before the property is seen, and you can say no.

sections.h2: Getting ready to sell a Marion house
sections.html:
Start with age. A house near the historic uptown core and one in a subdivision from the recent growth years are different products, and a buyer will weigh the roof, furnace and wiring in either. Write down when each was last replaced and keep any receipts.

Then settle your paperwork. Ask the Linn County Treasurer for the paid receipts, find payoff letters for any mortgage or lien, and, for a rental, locate the license and the last inspection results. If the house came through an estate, confirm the deed names match the people who will sign.

faqs.q: Do I need to register my Marion rental before I sell it?
faqs.a: Rentals must be registered and the landlord licensed. Notify the city once you no longer own the unit, and expect the new owner to register if they plan to rent. Marion Rental Housing, 319-200-1299, can confirm what applies to your address.

faqs.q: When are Linn County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are due September 1 and March 1. Delinquency starts October 1 and April 1, so a mailed check needs a September 30 or March 31 postmark.

faqs.q: What is the Iowa transfer tax on a house sale?
faqs.a: Iowa Code 428A.1 sets 80 cents per $500 of value beyond the first $500. The recorder collects it as the deed comes in, alongside the declaration of value.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Marion house in?
faqs.a: The street decides. Marion Independent has the south and east sides, Linn-Mar has the north, west and far east, and a few areas belong to the Cedar Rapids district.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Marion house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer takes the house as is, so a bad roof, foundation, water damage or old systems can stay unfixed. The offer accounts for the condition, and accepting is your call.
